observable_boundary.intrinsic_vs_lab: A nonzero intrinsic cranked current is a T-odd order parameter of an oriented mean-field solution. A good-I projected laboratory state is an eigenstate of J^2 and can be built by angular-momentum projection; it does not retain a classical direction vector as an observable.
observable_boundary.T_invariant_state: If the state itself is invariant under T, expectation of a T-odd current vanishes. Cranked TAC states are not T-invariant because the Routhian contains -omega dot J.
observable_boundary.S_invariant_state: An antiunitary S=T R_y(pi) can leave a nonzero intrinsic field invariant because rotation compensates the T sign. This is a relation of the full density/current field, not a pointwise statement that j=0.
observable_boundary.experiment: R_DCO/IPDCO, lifetimes, branching, absolute B(M1)/B(E2), S(I), alignment and partner mapping are laboratory observables; a residual on an arbitrary toy j(r) is none of these.

warnings: The 017 MR/AMR fields use arbitrary Gaussian vortices and do not solve an EDF or HFB equation.
The integrated AMR cancellation in this toy concerns a chosen orbital moment component; it does not prove AMR assignment or forbid all M1 matrix elements.
Rz(pi), T and T R_y(pi) labels depend on body-axis convention and operator parity; source conventions must be retained.
No residual value establishes MR, AMR or chirality in a nucleus.
